page.layout: Top: ornamental border; title block at upper left. Below it, the main text column on the left, with the woodcut initial and headings. A column of marginal notes runs down the right margin beside the text. Full-width text continues below the column. Footnotes in small type sit at the foot of the text block, full width.

main_text.head: DVODECIM TABVLARVM fragmenta.
LIBER PRIMVS.
De cultu diuino.
main_text.p: AD DIVOS adeunto caste{a} pietatem adhibento. opes{b} a-moueto. Qui secus faxit, Deus{c} ipse vindex{d} erit.Quæ leges hoc priore li-bro continen-tur, ex Ciceronis libris de legib[?] de-cerptæ, verè duodecim ta-bularum non sunt, sed à Ci-cerone par-tim inuentæ, partim ex i-psis legibus duodecim in-terpolatę. id-que Tullius ipse libro 3. de legibus, mini-me diffitetur. Non recognoscimus, inquit, nunc leges P. Romani, sed aut repetim-[?]ereptas, aut nouas scribi-mus. Fecit i-taque mixtu-
main_text.head: Qui colendi.
main_text.p: SEPARATIM nemo habessit{e} deos neve novos{f}: sed ne aduenas{g}, nisi publi-cè adscitos{h} priuatim colunto.
main_text.head: Vbi colendi.
main_text.p: CONSTRVCTA a patribus delu-[?]ra veterum legum, rerumque ipsarum vtilitas, vt eas lectori proponerem, non tam vt eas cognosceret, quàm ne ignorarét.
{c} nedum homo. & his quidem verbis, praesentis poenae metu reliqua confirmari videntur.
{d} lege prima, Codice de rebus credit.

{g} His verbis tollit confusionem religionum & ceremoniarum, Cicero. Diu certè hoc Romae seruatum non fuit. Testis erit dea Pessinuntia quae & mater deum, Phrygia aduecta non sine magnis miraculis, Herodianus 1: 18. Plin.3.

{h} Tertullianus 5 Apologet: Verus, inquit, erat decretum, ne quis Deus ab imperatore consecraretur, nisi à Senatu probaretur. & post, apud vos de humano arbitratu diuinitas pensitatur. Nisi homini Deus placuerit, Deus non erit. & post, Tiberi* nonne Christum detulerat ad senatum, cum praerogatiua suffragij sui? Senatus, quia ipse non probauerat, respuit: Eusebius 1[?]. hist.
2. id ea de causa factum fuisse refert, quod salutaris praedicatio nulla opus habeat humana approbatione.

page.notes: The woodcut initial "A" is followed by a small capital "D": read as AD DIVOS, the woodcut letter not fully certain. "delu-" at the foot of the column: the continuation in the margin ("mus.") does not fit, so the word is doubtful. The marginal note is printed beside the heading and the first paragraphs; it is placed at the start of the first paragraph. Two superscript marks in the margin (before "duodecim" and "que Tullius") and the superscript after "legib" and "repetim" are unclear and are not transcribed as marks. "Tiberi*" has an asterisk in the print. Footnote numbers "1." (Eusebius) and "21" (Paulus) are unclear. The page number "57" at top right is doubtful. No running head, catchword or signature is printed.
